source.title: The Role of Early Bioelectric Signals in the Regeneration of Planarian Anterior/Posterior Polarity.
source.location: Figure 2B legend (panels e-f) and Results text ('13% ... compared to 0% in controls ... remaining 87% ... normal single-headed'); doses from Methods

stage: trunk fragment (PT fragment: cut just posterior to the pharynx and halfway to the tail tip)
injury: two transverse amputations (immediately posterior to the pharynx; halfway to the tail tip)

intervention.duration: first 3 h postamputation, then washed 3x in water
intervention.description: PT fragments soaked in 0.24 uM nigericin with 15 mM potassium gluconate for the first 3 h after amputation, then washed

readout.method: dissecting-microscope scoring for at least one eye at each pole

notes: 13% double-headed; text states the remaining 87% were morphologically normal single-headed with no intermediate phenotypes. Legend gives N=132 for the Fisher's exact test; it is not explicit whether N is the treated arm alone or treated+control (17/132 = 12.9% fits treated-only), so percentages kept with n_total null and N recorded here. Dose field = nigericin; 15 mM potassium gluconate co-applied.

adjudication.note: B converted with N=132 as treated n; legend N belongs to the Fisher test and may include controls, so kept percentages (A)
